graph.name: coin-cell-led-perfboard
graph.description: Press the button, the LED lights: the circuit of coin-cell-led with through-hole parts, soldered on a perfboard.

purpose.notes: The example of the edakit handbook, chapter 17: built for oneself, a desk gadget for adults, kept out of the reach of small children – the cell comes out by hand (D-5).

components.label: CR2032 holder
components.notes: Through-hole holder lying flat, pins 20 mm apart: pin 1 = plus (Kinghelm KH-CR2032-2-1 drawing).

accept.LIM.i/cell: SW1 is pressed for a moment: while it is held a fresh cell gives up to 9.0 mA, above its 3 mA continuous and below its 15 mA pulse current (Jauch CR 2032 H2B); held longer it costs capacity and voltage, no harm – the voltage drop is in the simulation by the cell's r (D-7)

components.label: Push button
components.notes: 6 x 6 mm through-hole: pins 1/2 and 3/4 are connected inside.

components.label: LED series resistor
components.notes: 150 Ω as in the example: 1.9 mA from a used cell (2.5 V, 40 Ω) into D1 at its highest Vf, 9.0 mA from a fresh cell at its lowest (sim)

components.label: LED (red 5 mm)
components.notes: Red 5 mm: Vf 1.8–2.4 V at 20 mA (XINGLIGHT). Pin 1 is the anode, the square pad.

nets.name: VBAT
nets.notes: the cell: 3.0 V nominal, 3.2 V and a little more fresh off load; negative with the cell upside down

nets.name: LED_SW
nets.notes: the cell's voltage while SW1 is pressed

accept.PATH.reverse: a cell upside down drives R1 and D1 backwards: D1 blocks, 3.2 V against its VR of 5 V – sim scenario reversed/pressed (LIM.v reverse voltage, SIM.state LED dark); no other part on the board (D-3)

notes: the cell (Ø 20 mm) sits in BT1's recess under the clip at its + end and comes out at the round − end: keep that end free to lever it out
D1 next to SW1: the LED shows the press

accept.HINT.bulk: no cable and no plug: the cell sits in BT1 on the board, the only load is D1 (at most 11 mA)
accept.HINT.lithium: a CR2032 is a primary Li-MnO2 cell, not Li-ion: nothing on the board charges it (LIM.backfeed) and it is not recharged
